_meta.indication: Indicated to improve wakefulness in adult patients with excessive daytime sleepiness associated with narcolepsy or obstructive sleep apnea (OSA)

pivotal_trials.design: 12-week, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter, four-arm parallel group study; patients randomized to placebo or solriamfetol 75, 150, or 300 mg once daily
pivotal_trials.population: Adult patients with excessive daytime sleepiness associated with narcolepsy (ICSD-3 or DSM-5 criteria)
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Co-primary endpoints: change from baseline in Maintenance of Wakefulness Test (MWT) and Epworth Sleepiness Scale (ESS) at Week 12
pivotal_trials.result: At 150 mg, statistically significant improvements vs placebo on MWT (treatment effect difference 7.7 minutes) and ESS (difference 3.8 points) at Week 12

pivotal_trials.design: 12-week, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter, five-arm parallel group study; solriamfetol 37.5, 75, 150, 300 mg or placebo daily in a 1:1:2:2:2 ratio
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with excessive daytime sleepiness associated with obstructive sleep apnea diagnosed per ICSD-3 criteria
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Co-primary endpoints: change from baseline in MWT and ESS at Week 12
pivotal_trials.result: Statistically significant improvements vs placebo on MWT (treatment effect differences 4.5, 8.9, and 10.7 minutes at 37.5, 75, 150 mg) and ESS (1.9, 1.7, and 4.5 points) at Week 12

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (incidence >=5% and greater than placebo): headache, nausea, decreased appetite, insomnia, and anxiety. Major safety concern is dose-dependent increases in systolic/diastolic blood pressure and heart rate.
target_moa: Solriamfetol is a dopamine and norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor (DNRI); its wake-promoting efficacy is thought to be mediated by inhibition of dopamine and norepinephrine reuptake

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee meeting was held for this application

summary.text: Standard NDA (505(b)) approved March 20, 2019 for solriamfetol, a new molecular entity, to improve wakefulness in EDS associated with narcolepsy or OSA; the narcolepsy indication had orphan drug designation. No advisory committee was convened.

citations.quote: Solriamfetol is a new molecular entity for the treatment of excessive daytime sleepiness (EDS) in patients with narcolepsy and patients with obstructive sleep apnea (OSA). Excessive daytime sleepiness is a prominent symptom of these conditions. requirement.text: A prospective, registry based observational exposure cohort study comparing maternal, fetal, and infant outcomes of women exposed to solriamfetol during pregnancy to an unexposed control population (pregnancy registry)

citations.quote: 3475-1 A prospective, registry based observational exposure cohort study that compares the maternal, fetal, and infant outcomes of women exposed to solriamfetol during pregnancy to an unexposed control population. The registry will detect and record major and minor congenital malformations, spontaneous abortions, stillbirths, elective terminations, small for gestational age, preterm birth, and any other adverse pregnancy outcomes. These outcomes will be assessed throughout pregnancy. Infant outcomes, including effects on postnatal growth and development, will be assessed through at least the first year of life.

requirement.text: An additional pregnancy study using a different design from the pregnancy registry to assess major congenital malformations, spontaneous abortions, stillbirths, small for gestational age and preterm birth in exposed vs unexposed women

citations.quote: 3475-2 An additional pregnancy study that uses a different design from the Pregnancy Registry (for example a retrospective cohort study using claims or electronic medical record data with outcome validation or a case control study) to assess major congenital malformations, spontaneous abortions, stillbirths, and small for gestational age and preterm birth in women exposed to solriamfetol during pregnancy compared to an unexposed control population.

requirement.text: A lactation study (milk only) in lactating women receiving therapeutic doses of solriamfetol to assess drug concentrations in breast milk and effects on the breastfed infant

citations.quote: 3475-3 Perform a lactation study (milk only) in lactating women who have received therapeutic doses of solriamfetol using a validated assay to assess concentrations of solriamfetol in breast milk and the effects on the breastfed infant.
